title: sorry 和 excuse me 到底差在哪
title_en: Sorry or Excuse Me? It's All About Timing
summary_zh: sorry 和 excuse me 经常被混用，其实关键在“时间点”：一个用在打扰别人之前，一个用在事情发生之后。读完你会知道什么场合该说哪一个。
body: Many learners use "sorry" and "excuse me" as if they meant the same thing, but in everyday English the choice often depends on timing. "Excuse me" usually comes before you do something that might bother someone. If you need to get past a person on a busy train, you say "excuse me". If you want to ask a stranger for directions, you start the same way. "Sorry", on the other hand, usually comes after something has already happened. You step on someone's foot, so you say "sorry". You miss what a friend said, so you say "Sorry?" with a rising voice, which asks them to repeat it. Things get more interesting when the two words overlap. Some people say "sorry" when someone else bumps into them, even when it clearly wasn't their fault. In that case, "sorry" isn't really an apology; it's more like a quick way of keeping the peace. A simple rule can help: "excuse me" opens a door, and "sorry" closes one. When you aren't sure, choose either one and say it with a smile. Being friendly matters more than picking the perfect word.

questions.prompt: What is the main difference between the two phrases, according to the text?
options: "Excuse me" is more polite than "sorry" in every situation
"Excuse me" is for strangers, while "sorry" is for friends
"Excuse me" usually comes before an action, while "sorry" usually comes after
"Sorry" should only be used for serious mistakes
questions.evidence: "Excuse me" usually comes before you do something that might bother someone.

questions.prompt: In the text, what does "keeping the peace" mean?
options: Staying completely silent in public
Telling someone politely that they made a mistake
Asking someone to move out of the way
Avoiding a small moment of tension between people
questions.evidence: it's more like a quick way of keeping the peace

questions.prompt: What does the rule "excuse me opens a door, and sorry closes one" mean?
options: "Excuse me" starts an interaction, and "sorry" ends a small problem
You should say sorry when you leave a room
You should say excuse me at every door
Both phrases are only used at doors
questions.evidence: "Excuse me" usually comes before you do something that might bother someone.

questions.prompt: How can you ask someone to repeat what they said, according to the text?
options: Say "Sorry?" with a rising voice
Wave your hand
Say "Pardon me" slowly
Say "Excuse me" loudly
questions.evidence: you say "Sorry?" with a rising voice

vocabulary.example: I'm sorry to bother you, but is this seat free?
A stranger helped me carry my bags up the stairs.
Our holidays overlap by two days, so we can travel together.
He sent a short apology for missing the meeting.

expressions.note: 在拥挤的地方请别人让一让：Can I just get past?
对比两种情况时的连接语，常放在句中、用逗号隔开
step on 表示“踩到”，地铁、排队时常用
既可以是身体撞到，也可以是“偶遇”：I bumped into Lily at the shop.
指为了不起冲突而做的小让步，常用 a way of keeping the peace
matter 作动词表示“要紧”：What matters most is...

knowledge.quote: If you need to get past a person on a busy train, you say "excuse me".
knowledge.explanation: 真实条件句描述“遇到这种情况通常怎么做”：if 从句和主句都用一般现在时，很适合讲规则和习惯。

knowledge.quote: Some people say "sorry" when someone else bumps into them, even when it clearly wasn't their fault.
knowledge.explanation: when 引导时间状语从句；even when 表示“即使在……的时候”，强调出乎意料，比单用 when 语气更强。

knowledge.quote: Being friendly matters more than picking the perfect word.
knowledge.explanation: 动名词 Being friendly 作主语，than 后面也用动名词 picking，前后结构保持一致，读起来更顺。

speaking: 用 1 分钟描述三个场景：地铁上要下车、没听清别人的话、不小心碰到别人。分别说出你会用 excuse me 还是 sorry，并解释原因。
writing: 写 80–100 词，比较中文里“不好意思”和“对不起”的用法，看看和英文的 excuse me / sorry 有什么相同和不同。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 A opens a door, and B closes one 的对比结构，总结两个容易混淆的词或做法。
task.model: "excuse me" opens a door, and "sorry" closes one

title: 一个讲不通的笑话
title_en: The Joke That Was About a Fish
summary_zh: 在宿舍聚餐上，“我”把爷爷最爱的中文笑话翻成英文，结果全场安静——因为笑点是一个谐音。读完你会看到笑话为什么难翻译，以及一个失败的笑话如何变成朋友间的“梗”。
body: At our first dinner in the shared flat, everyone agreed to bring a joke from home. When it was my turn, I chose my grandfather's favourite one, which always makes my family cry with laughter. I translated it carefully and delivered the last line with a big smile. Nobody laughed. There was a long, polite silence, and then Priya asked kindly whether there was a second part. Too late, I realised that the whole joke depended on two Chinese words that sound exactly the same: one means fish, and the other means having more than enough. In English, it was just a strange sentence about a fish. So I explained it slowly, with drawings on a paper napkin. By the time I finished, everyone was laughing, but not at the joke. They were laughing at how hard I was trying. Then Diego told a joke from Chile, and it failed in exactly the same way. Since that night, we have had a running joke of our own. Whenever something gets lost in translation, someone whispers "fish", and the whole table loses it.

questions.prompt: Why did nobody laugh when the writer first told the joke?
options: The writer forgot the most important line
The joke was about a topic the others found sad
The others could not understand the writer's accent
The joke worked only because of how two Chinese words sound
questions.evidence: the whole joke depended on two Chinese words that sound exactly the same

questions.prompt: What does "the whole table loses it" most likely mean?
options: Everyone at the table gets angry
Everyone at the table bursts out laughing
Everyone at the table forgets the joke
Everyone at the table leaves the room
questions.evidence: someone whispers "fish", and the whole table loses it

questions.prompt: Why were people laughing after the writer explained the joke?
options: They found the writer's effort funny and charming
They finally understood the Chinese words
The drawings were very silly
Diego had told a better joke
questions.evidence: They were laughing at how hard I was trying.

questions.prompt: What did the writer use to explain the joke?
options: A short video
Drawings on a paper napkin
A translation app
A Chinese dictionary
questions.evidence: with drawings on a paper napkin

vocabulary.example: She delivered her speech without looking at her notes.
After the question, there was a short silence.
Our plans depended on the weather.
My brother always whispers during films.

expressions.note: 形容笑得特别厉害，比 laugh a lot 生动得多
It's your turn. 轮到你了；讲游戏、发言顺序都常用

expressions.meaning: 等我反应过来已经晚了
expressions.note: Too late 放句首，带一点懊恼，讲故事时很自然
指一群人之间长期流传、一提就笑的笑话
可以指语言翻译，也可以指沟通中意思没传到
口语，要看上下文：笑场或发火都可以用

knowledge.quote: I chose my grandfather's favourite one, which always makes my family cry with laughter.
knowledge.explanation: 逗号 + which 引导非限制性定语从句，给前面的 one（那个笑话）补充信息；去掉从句，主句意思依然完整。

knowledge.quote: Since that night, we have had a running joke of our own.
knowledge.explanation: since + 过去的时间点，主句用现在完成时 have had，表示从那时起一直持续到现在的状态。

knowledge.quote: Priya asked kindly whether there was a second part
knowledge.explanation: whether 引导宾语从句，转述一个一般疑问句；从句用陈述语序 there was，不能写成 was there。

speaking: 用 1 分钟讲一个你觉得很难翻译成英文的中文笑话或说法：它好笑在哪里，为什么翻译之后就不好笑了。
writing: 写 100–120 词，讲一次你和朋友之间产生“梗”的经历：当时发生了什么，现在大家怎么用它。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 Since..., we have had... 说说一件事给你和朋友留下的“梗”或习惯。
task.model: Since that night, we have had a running joke of our own.

title: 礼物为什么没当面拆
title_en: Why Didn't You Open My Present?
summary_zh: Hannah 送的生日礼物，Jun 没有当场拆开，她担心了一整天。两人一聊才发现，两家的习惯正好相反。读完你能学会用英语坦诚地化解一个小误会。
body: Hannah: Jun, can I ask you about last night? Jun: Sure, is everything okay? Hannah: It's probably silly, but you didn't open my present. I've been wondering all day whether you liked it. Jun: Oh no, I opened it as soon as I got home! The tea set is beautiful. Hannah: Really? Then why did you put it away so quickly? Jun: In my family, we usually wait until the guests leave. If you tear the paper open in front of everyone, it can look a bit greedy, as if the gift matters more than the person. Hannah: That's funny, because in my family it's the opposite. Unless you open a present right away, people think you're not interested. Jun: I had no idea that waiting could look rude. So we were both trying to be polite. Hannah: Just in completely different ways! Jun: Next time, I'll open it in front of you and make a big fuss about it. Hannah: Deal, and I'll try not to stare at the box all evening.

questions.prompt: What caused the misunderstanding between Hannah and Jun?
options: Jun didn't like the tea set very much
Hannah gave Jun the present too late
Their families have opposite habits about opening presents
Jun opened the present before the guests arrived
questions.evidence: That's funny, because in my family it's the opposite.

questions.prompt: Why does Jun's family usually wait before opening presents?
options: Opening them at once can look greedy
They prefer to open presents on a special day
They like to write thank-you notes first
They don't want to waste the wrapping paper
questions.evidence: it can look a bit greedy, as if the gift matters more than the person

questions.prompt: What does Hannah mean by "Just in completely different ways!"?
options: They both wanted to leave early
They both forgot about the present
They both disliked the present
Both were being polite according to their own family habits
questions.evidence: So we were both trying to be polite.

questions.prompt: What does "make a big fuss about it" mean?
options: complain loudly
hide it away
forget about it
show a lot of excitement and attention
questions.evidence: make a big fuss about it

vocabulary.example: Don't be greedy, leave some cake for the others.
I thought he was shy, but he's the opposite.
It's polite to say hello when you walk into a small shop.
Try not to stare at people on the train.

expressions.note: 提出一个小担心前先“降低姿态”，让对方不觉得被指责

expressions.text: as soon as I got home
expressions.note: as soon as 表示“一……就……”，讲两件紧挨着发生的事
put away 收好、放回原处；代词要放中间：put it away
口语里比 immediately 更常用

expressions.text: make a big fuss about it
expressions.meaning: 大张旗鼓地表示（惊喜、感谢）
expressions.note: make a fuss about 可以是热情夸张，也可以是“小题大做”，看语境

knowledge.quote: I've been wondering all day whether you liked it.
knowledge.explanation: have been + -ing 是现在完成进行时，表示从早上到现在一直在想、而且还没停，比 I wondered 更能表达“担心了一整天”。

knowledge.quote: Unless you open a present right away, people think you're not interested.
knowledge.explanation: unless = if... not，“除非马上拆开，否则……”。unless 从句本身用肯定形式，不要再加 not。

knowledge.quote: I had no idea that waiting could look rude.
knowledge.explanation: that 从句跟在 idea 后面，说明“什么想法”，是同位语从句；have no idea that... 表示“完全没想到……”。

speaking: 和同伴演一段 1 分钟的对话：一方因为某个小习惯误会了另一方，用 It's probably silly, but... 开口，最后两人把话说开。
writing: 写 100–120 词，讲一次你在送礼或收礼时遇到的小误会，以及你们后来是怎么说清楚的。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 Unless you..., people think... 说说你身边一个“不这样做就会被误会”的小习惯。
task.model: Unless you open a present right away, people think you're not interested.

title: 跟奶奶学剪纸
summary_zh: 采访一位跟奶奶学剪纸的年轻人：从“剪出来像断腿蜘蛛”到自己开班教小朋友。读完你会学到描述“学一门手艺”的实用表达。
body: Q: How did you start paper-cutting? Xiaowen: My grandmother taught me when I was about ten. Every winter, she cut red patterns to stick on our windows, and I wanted to help. Q: Was it hard to learn? Xiaowen: Very! My first flowers looked like broken spiders. She made me practise the same simple shape again and again before I could try anything new. Q: What's the most important thing she taught you? Xiaowen: To be patient with the paper. You can't rush a curve. If your hand is nervous, the scissors know it. Q: Do you still cut with her? Xiaowen: We haven't sat at the same table for a while, because she lives in another city now. But we video call every Sunday, and she checks my work through the screen. She still finds tiny mistakes that I can't see. Q: Have you taught anyone else? Xiaowen: Yes, I've started a small class for children in my neighbourhood. Some of them get bored quickly, but one quiet girl, who hardly ever speaks in class, always stays behind to cut one more.

questions.prompt: What is the most important lesson Xiaowen learned from her grandmother?
options: Paper-cutting should be done as quickly as possible
Beginners should only use red paper
Good work needs patience and a lot of practice
Simple shapes are more beautiful than complex ones
questions.evidence: To be patient with the paper.

questions.prompt: How does her grandmother help her today?
options: She checks Xiaowen's work during video calls
She visits Xiaowen's class every Sunday
She sends Xiaowen new patterns by post
She cuts shapes for Xiaowen's students
questions.evidence: she checks my work through the screen

questions.prompt: What does "If your hand is nervous, the scissors know it" suggest?
options: Paper-cutting is dangerous
Scissors can feel emotions
Nervousness shows in your cutting, so you need to stay calm
You should buy better scissors

questions.prompt: What does "stays behind" mean in "always stays behind to cut one more"?
options: arrives late
remains after the others have left
sits at the back
goes home early
questions.evidence: always stays behind to cut one more

vocabulary.example: The plates have blue patterns around the edge.
I practise the piano for twenty minutes every evening.
Slow down before the curve in the road.
Can I borrow your scissors for a second?

expressions.note: 强调反复练习或发生，比 many times 更有画面感
后面可以接人，也可以接事物：be patient with yourself
You can't rush + 某事：说某件事必须慢慢来
常和完成时连用：I haven't seen him for a while.
get + 形容词表示状态变化：get tired, get bored
常说下课、下班后留下：stay behind after class

knowledge.quote: she cut red patterns to stick on our windows
knowledge.explanation: to stick 是不定式表示目的，说明剪窗花是“为了贴到窗户上”；目的状语放在句末最常见。

knowledge.quote: We haven't sat at the same table for a while
knowledge.explanation: 现在完成时否定 + for a while，表示“已经有一段时间没有……”，强调从过去到现在的一段空白。

knowledge.quote: one quiet girl, who hardly ever speaks in class, always stays behind to cut one more
knowledge.explanation: who 引导非限制性定语从句，插在主语和谓语之间补充说明这个女孩；注意主句谓语 stays 仍然和 girl 保持一致。

speaking: 用 1 分钟讲讲你跟长辈学过的一样本事（做菜、写毛笔字、修东西都可以）：谁教的、最难的地方、学到的道理。
writing: 假设你要采访一位会传统手艺的长辈，用英文写出 5 个问题，并为其中两个写出你猜测的回答（共 100–120 词）。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 You can't rush... 说一件你认为“急不来”的事。
